text:
omar: Hey all, quick onboarding kubectl question. I ran the usual `aws sso login` + `aws eks update-kubeconfig --name redwood-dev --region us-east-1 --profile redwood-onboard` but `kubectl get pods -n omar-dev` returns Forbidden. Thoughts?

diane: welcome! usually that means you don't have a RoleBinding in your namespace. Which context does `kubectl config current-context` show?

omar: it shows `arn:aws:eks:us-east-1:123456789012:cluster/redwood-dev`. The kubeconfig's user exec is `aws eks get-token` with profile redwood-onboard.

diane: yep that's the SSO helper. File the Kubernetes access form and request `namespace=omar-dev` with role `onboard-edit`. Infra will create a namespaced RoleBinding.

omar: where's the form? I don't see it in the handbook.

tom: https://redwood.example.com/access -> choose "Kubernetes namespace access". Put the namespace and request `onboard-edit`. If you need a faster temporary workaround we sometimes create a ServiceAccount and give you a kubeconfig tied to it (support ticket).

infra-bot: access request created by omar at 1968000006  id K-10888. Assigned to infra team. ETA ~1h.

omar: thanks, filed it. small question: do I need to re-run `aws sso login` after infra approves?

diane: yes — re-run `aws sso login --profile redwood-onboard` so the SSO session picks up the new role mapping, then `aws eks get-token` will return a token with the bound role. After that `kubectl get pods -n omar-dev` should work.

omar: update: infra approved, re-ran `aws sso login` and `kubectl get pods -n omar-dev` works now. leaving my tiny snippet for others: `alias kctxn='kubectl config set-context --current --namespace'`

tom: nice! glad it worked. :party_parrot:
